items.headline: Singapore becomes a 'super-aged' society as population hits a record 6.21 million
items.summary: The Population in Brief 2026 report, released on Sep 25, put the total population up 1.6% to 6.21 million as of June, with citizens aged 65 and above now 21.4% of the citizen population, crossing the UN 'super-aged' threshold. Non-residents rose 3.7% to 1.98 million.

items.headline: Five charged over a S$155,600 'bump-and-steal' theft near Orchard's Tang Plaza
items.summary: Tanglin Police arrested five Filipino nationals, aged 31 to 57, after a man who had just changed currency was jostled at an escalator near Tang Plaza and had about S$155,600 taken from his bag. Around S$152,800 was recovered, and all five were charged on Sep 26 with theft with common intention.

items.headline: Man, 50, charged after a fire is set at the entrance of a Raffles Place mosque
items.summary: Police were alerted to a fire outside Masjid Moulana Mohamed Ali at 80 Raffles Place (UOB Plaza) at about 9pm on Sep 25; a preliminary probe found a man had placed an oil tin at the entrance and set an undergarment alight before leaving. A member of the public put it out, no one was hurt, and the man was charged on Sep 26.

items.headline: Haze returns as central Singapore's 24-hour PSI enters the unhealthy range
items.summary: Air quality in central Singapore crossed into the unhealthy band on Sep 26, with the 24-hour PSI reaching 106, the first such breach in almost a week. The NEA attributed it to smoke from fires in southern Sumatra and Kalimantan drifting in on the prevailing winds.

items.headline: India's forex reserves post their biggest weekly drop in two years as the RBI defends the rupee
items.summary: India's foreign-exchange reserves fell by US$14.88 billion to US$765.9 billion in the week to Sep 18, the largest weekly decline since November 2024, after the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars to support a rupee pressured by higher oil prices and portfolio outflows.

items.headline: India's SEBI clears portfolio managers to invest overseas and short equity options
items.summary: India's market regulator SEBI approved rules on Sep 25 allowing portfolio managers to invest client money abroad and take short positions in equity options, part of a package aimed at widening investment choices even as foreign investors keep trimming Indian holdings.

items.headline: Palestine Action supporters plan a mass vigil at Burnham's first Labour conference
items.summary: Organisers said a 'mass, silent sign-holding vigil' would gather near the Labour conference venue in Liverpool on Sep 26, the first party conference over which Prime Minister Andy Burnham presides, in protest at the government's proscription of the group Palestine Action.

items.headline: Trump hosts Xi with fanfare, but the China-US summit yields little of substance
items.summary: President Donald Trump welcomed Xi Jinping to Washington on Sep 24 with elaborate ceremony, extending a trade truce and floating cooperation on AI risks, but the meeting produced few concrete outcomes on the tensions between the world's two largest economies.

items.headline: Russia and Germany's foreign ministers hold their first talks since the 2022 invasion
items.summary: Sergey Lavrov and Johann Wadephul met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Sep 26, the first such Russia-Germany talks since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine; Berlin pressed Moscow to help revive Black Sea grain and energy exports.

items.headline: Swiss voters decide whether to lock 'perpetual, armed' neutrality into the constitution
items.summary: Switzerland votes on Sep 27 on an SVP-backed initiative that would bar military cooperation with alliances unless the country is attacked and ban unilateral sanctions; a 'yes' could force Bern to unwind its Russia sanctions, though pre-vote polls showed 63-68% opposed.

items.headline: France to send troops and air defences to protect the Saudi oil port of Yanbu
items.summary: President Emmanuel Macron said France would deploy soldiers, radar and defence systems to protect Saudi Arabia's Red Sea crude terminal at Yanbu after repeated Houthi missile strikes, insisting the move was to guard the site rather than join the conflict.

items.headline: 'Model drop week': Anthropic ships Opus 5.5, OpenAI counters with GPT-6 within the hour
items.summary: Anthropic released Opus 5.5 on Sep 22, cheaper at US$20 per million output tokens and claiming state-of-the-art coding performance, and OpenAI launched GPT-6 'Sol' and 'Luna' about 90 minutes later, the back-to-back releases quickly dubbed 'model drop week.'

items.headline: British AI 'neocloud' Nscale secures $3.36 billion ahead of its US IPO
items.summary: Nscale raised US$3.36 billion in convertible financing led by hedge fund Third Point, with US$2.36 billion available immediately and US$1 billion from existing investor Nvidia, ahead of a planned US listing later this year.

items.headline: Meta debuts camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio AI glasses at $349
items.summary: At its Connect conference Meta unveiled its first camera-free smart glasses, the 43-gram Ray-Ban Meta Audio, starting at US$349 with up to 12 hours of battery, positioned as a cheaper entry point to its wearables line; they ship Oct 13.

items.headline: AI drone maker Tekever raises $580 million at a $6.4 billion valuation
items.summary: Portuguese-British defence-tech firm Tekever announced the first close of a US$580 million Series D led by UC Investments and Baillie Gifford, roughly quadrupling its valuation to US$6.4 billion, days after winning a UK Army surveillance contract worth up to 400 million pounds.

items.headline: US consumer sentiment slides to a four-month low as inflation fears deepen
items.summary: The University of Michigan's final September sentiment index fell to 48.1 from 51.7 in August, a four-month low, while year-ahead inflation expectations climbed to 4.6%, the highest since June, underscoring household anxiety over prices.

items.headline: RNAi biotech ADARx raises $446 million in an upsized Nasdaq IPO backed by AbbVie
items.summary: ADARx Pharmaceuticals priced its IPO at US$17 a share, the top of its range, selling 26.25 million shares to raise US$446.3 million; it began trading on Sep 25 as 'ADRX,' with AbbVie committing up to US$100 million in a concurrent private placement.

items.headline: Darden profit slips as Olive Garden growth cools despite a 5.1% sales rise
items.summary: Darden Restaurants posted fiscal first-quarter EPS of US$2.04, down from US$2.19 a year earlier, on sales up 5.1% to US$3.2 billion; Olive Garden same-restaurant sales grew just 1.1% while LongHorn Steakhouse gained 6.2%, sending shares down about 3%.

items.headline: Saudi crude exports hit their highest since the Iran war began, despite a pipeline outage
items.summary: Kpler data showed Saudi crude exports running near 6 million barrels a day in September, the highest since the roughly seven-month-old Iran conflict began, even after Riyadh shut its damaged East-West pipeline and rerouted barrels through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Russell holds off Verstappen by a tenth to win a chaotic Azerbaijan Grand Prix
items.summary: George Russell converted pole into his third win of the season, crossing the line just 0.196 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen in a Baku race that saw six retirements, including Lando Norris after a Franco Colapinto collision. Russell had earlier taken pole by eight tenths.

items.headline: Isack Hadjar's P3 seals Red Bull's first double podium since 2024
items.summary: Isack Hadjar finished third in Baku to give Red Bull its first double podium since the 2024 Chinese Grand Prix, capping a comeback after the rookie missed three races with a wrist injury; championship leader Kimi Antonelli recovered from a Q1 crash to fifth.

items.headline: Fernandez fights back past Chwalinska to reach the Singapore Open final
items.summary: Leylah Fernandez dropped the opening set before beating Poland's Maja Chwalinska 1-6, 6-4, 6-2 to reach her first tour-level final of the season at the Singapore Tennis Open, with the title match set for Sunday.

items.headline: Asian Games men's cricket quarter-finals set, with India drawn against Afghanistan
items.summary: Rain washed out the last group matches on Sep 26, sending Nepal, Afghanistan, Malaysia and Hong Kong through and setting up the Sep 28 quarter-finals: India v Afghanistan, Pakistan v Hong Kong, Sri Lanka v Nepal and Bangladesh v Malaysia.

items.headline: Physicists drive antimatter down a road for the first time in a CERN world first
items.summary: The BASE collaboration reported in Nature that it sealed 92 antiprotons in a portable Penning trap and trucked them 7.5 km across CERN's campus with no losses, a proof of concept for moving antimatter to quieter labs, expected to enable up to 100-fold more precise tests of matter-antimatter symmetry.

fun_fact.headline: Tardigrades are the only animals known to survive the vacuum of space.
fun_fact.body: Tardigrades, microscopic 'water bears' under a millimetre long, are the only animals known to have survived the open vacuum of space. In a 2007 European Space Agency experiment aboard the FOTON-M3 mission, dehydrated tardigrades were exposed to space vacuum and cosmic radiation for 10 days, and many revived once rehydrated on Earth, with some laying viable eggs. They endure by curling into a dried 'tun' state that all but shuts down their metabolism.

puzzle.title: Off by One
puzzle.body: A matchstick equation uses digits drawn like a digital clock (seven-segment style), with the plus and equals signs also made of matchsticks. It reads 5 + 7 = 2, which is false. Move exactly ONE matchstick (take none away, add none) so the equation becomes true.
puzzle.approach: You do not have to change a digit's value head-on; the operator is built from matchsticks too.
puzzle.answer: 9 - 7 = 2. Lift the vertical matchstick out of the '+' sign (turning it into a '-') and place it on the top-right of the '5', turning the 5 into a 9. The line now reads 9 - 7 = 2.

word_puzzle.title: Take Root
word_puzzle.body: Spelling Bee. Centre letter T (must appear in every word). All letters: A D E L N P T. Make words of four or more letters, reusing letters freely; at least one pangram uses all seven letters.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must include the centre letter T and use only the seven letters shown; find the seven-letter pangram first.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: PLANTED. Other valid words: PLANET, PLANT, PLATE, PLATED, PLEAT, TALENT, DENTAL, PEDANT, PALATE, ELATE, ELATED, DATE, DATED, TAPE, TAPED, LATE, NEAT, PEAT, TEAL.
